chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a man came to him. So he said to me: 'Do you love him?' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me: 'And why should you not love him, while he is your brother, and your partner in your religion, and your helper against your enemy, whereas his sustenance is upon someone else?'
ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims love each other according to the Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the believer's brotherhood not merely as a spiritual ideal but as a tangible social contract involving mutual aid and shared destiny. The Imam emphasizes that this bond serves as a practical support system against adversaries and a source of sustenance, reinforcing the Shia concept of *al-wala'* (loyalty) within the community. This highlights the interplay between spiritual affinity and material solidarity in maintaining the cohesion of the *Ummah*.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and a man came over to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do you love him<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And why should you not love him and he is your brother, and your associate in your religion, and your assistant against your enemy, whereas his sustenance is upon someone else!!’
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) when a man came in and the Imam asked me, ‘Do you love him?’ I said, ‘Yes, I love him.’ The Imam asked me, ‘How would you not love him when he is your brother (in belief), your partner in religion, your supporter against your enemies and someone other than you provides his sustenance?”’
